modifications: Replace root script aliases and independent parsers with one explicit command family, inclusive dates, offline inspection and no argument abbreviation.

Route standalone lineage and pricing refresh through durable registration before dependency acquisition. Expose offline producer status and return nonzero when required local processing is incomplete.
Apply shared durable work and complete-group restrictions to standalone lineage and pricing commands; require explicit retry authorization through daily update.

Resolve every new producer --through cutoff through the shared completed-session resolver before selection, registration or acquisition; report the requested date and effective trading session. Apply the same rule to preview, universe reconciliation, standalone pricing/lineage and combined catalogue construction while preserving reader filters and pinned resume inputs.
Always show phase completion and failure callbacks even when they arrive inside the progress throttle window, preserving final request counts and short-phase visibility.
Make catalogue commands operate on the standalone serving store, add explicit offline bootstrap/rebuild/preview, and move retained combined workflow commands under legacy catalogue.
Limit automatic serving maintenance after focused lineage commands to their selected complete groups, leaving unrelated pending catalogue work untouched.
Remove the legacy command family and unused monthly, clean-room and ticker workflows, retaining the current standalone commands and shared identity and source-selection rules.
Add offline CSV export by online public identity with an optional catalogue-only plan, explicit identity and date selection, per-identity digests and one final export manifest.

Report CSV operation lifecycles as bounded, versioned compact JSONL on STDERR with immediate INIT, sampled in-memory status, independent monotonic heartbeat intervals of 60/120/180/240/300 seconds then 300 seconds, and an optional fixed interval.
Emit immediate structured errors and exactly one FINAL_EXIT on controlled termination, isolate reporting failures from operation outcomes, and retain JSON results on STDOUT.
Add CSV --workers with choices 1 through 4, defaulting to 2, and report configured concurrency in plans and progress while keeping one lifecycle per export.
Remove CSV --wait: busy source or destination locks fail immediately with the existing busy exit code.
Return each CSV run's self-contained final manifest inside its timestamp directory instead of maintaining a shared export-root selector.

Serialize every store-writing command with one nonblocking exclusive store operation lock, and hold the matching shared lock across each CSV export so updates, other writers and exports cannot overlap incompatibly.

Advance lifecycle progress and error schemas to version 2, adding next_heart_beat_in_seconds to every envelope: seconds until the next scheduled heartbeat rounded up, or null for terminal error and FINAL_EXIT records.
Advance lifecycle schemas to version 3 and include ai_agent_read_this monitoring guidance only in the initial INIT envelope, never in subsequent heartbeats or terminal records.
Update the INIT message to announce that the CSV Exporter system has successfully started and suggest reporting this to the user where relevant.

Advance lifecycle schemas to version 4, add an initial 10-second heartbeat interval before the existing 60/120/180/240/300-second intervals while retaining fixed overrides, and report CSV estimated_remaining_seconds as TBD until an estimate is available.
Always display estimated_remaining_seconds as TBD in the initial 10-second heartbeat, regardless of phase or an already available estimate; preserve the held estimate for subsequent heartbeats.
Extend INIT-only ai_agent_read_this guidance to update the user only at each heartbeat unless the user directs otherwise.
Add a dedicated offline lineage policy-migration command that promotes only the exact completed policy transition without constructing provider clients or entering live lineage evaluation.
